title: Vientiane International Marathon 2026 Review: What the 2025 Race Was Like
seo_title: Vientiane International Marathon Review: Course, Weather, Roads
meta_description: Vientiane International Marathon review: 7,000+ runners in 2025, a 3.30am start from the That Luang grounds, 20°C at 6am, water every 2 km, and open roads.
dek: What the Laos capital's marathon is like, from the fifth edition in December 2025: the out-and-back course along the Mekong, a cool and misty morning, cut-offs, roads that stay open to traffic, and race-weekend logistics.
verdict: Enter if you want an unhurried capital-city marathon in cool December air and you are comfortable finishing on open roads. The 2025 race had more than 7,000 starters from 45 nationalities. At 6am Vientiane's airport recorded 20°C with a dew point of 17°C, cool for Southeast Asia, and it was only 23°C by 10am. The route runs out and back along the Mekong from the That Luang grounds, with water every 2 km and a six-and-a-half-hour marathon limit. The catch is traffic: the roads are not closed, and the organiser's 2024 rules reopen them fully at 6.30am, three hours into the marathon. If you are slower than that, expect cars for the rest of the race.

sections.heading: The 2025 Race: A Field That Grew by Half
paragraphs: The fifth Vientiane International Marathon was run on Sunday 14 December 2025, over a marathon, half marathon, 10 km and 5 km [1][2]. The Laotian Times reported more than 7,000 runners at the start from 45 nationalities, up 56% on about 4,500 in 2024, and called it Laos' biggest annual marathon event [1]. Dariusz Bemben of Poland won the men's marathon and Napatsorn Panthatawewit of Thailand the women's [1].

The race is organised by Events for Good (EFG) Laos [3]. Its presenting sponsor for a fifth year was Lao Brewery Company, through its Tigerhead water and Revive isotonic brands; the company said it made sure all runners had drinks throughout the race [1].

sections.heading: The Course: Out and Back Along the Mekong From That Luang
paragraphs: The race starts and finishes at the That Luang grounds [3][4], where 2025 race packs were also collected [2]. The organiser's 2024 and 2026 maps show the same routes [4][5]. The marathon heads down Lane Xang Avenue past the Patuxay monument to Rue Samsenthai, runs west along the Mekong to a turn beside Wattay International Airport at about 7 km, and comes back past the Chao Fa Ngum statue at 10 km. It then runs south along Donchan Road and Bor O Road to a second turn at 20 km, loops east and north past Setthathirath Hospital at around 28 to 30 km and along Phonpapao Road at 32 km, and returns through the centre to the finish [4].

The half marathon follows the same line down Lane Xang Avenue to the airport turn, then runs the Mekong waterfront past the King Anouvong statue to a turn by the Landmark Hotel at 14 km before heading back up Lane Xang Avenue [6]. The maps mark water every 2 km and first-aid points along the route, and carry a certified-measured-course logo from World Athletics and AIMS [4][6][5].

sections.heading: The Weather: Cool and Misty
paragraphs: Wattay International Airport, about 7 km west of the start and beside the course's first turn [4], has no archived readings between midnight and 6am on race day [7]. Its last reading before the 3.30am marathon start was 22°C and 78% humidity at 11.30pm, after rain and drizzle in the early evening [8]. At 6am it was 20°C, with a dew point of 17°C, 83% humidity, mist and a 2-knot wind. It was still 20°C at 7am, 22°C at 8am and 23°C at 10am, with 78% humidity [7].

A dew point of 17°C is comfortable by the region's standards, and a marathoner finishing inside the limit never ran in more than 23°C at the airport [7]. Mist was reported late on the evening before and again from 6am to 7.30am [7][8], on a course that starts at 3.30am on open roads.

sections.heading: The Roads and the Cut-offs
paragraphs: The race is run on public roads. The organiser's 2024 rules say the route is shared during the race until 6.30am, after which "the road will be fully reopened to live traffic" [3]. That is three hours into the marathon and two hours into the half, so under those rules most marathoners finish with traffic back on the roads. The same rules disclaim any warranty on the road surface, lighting, traffic restrictions, or members of the public and animals on the course [3].
A runner at the 2022 race quit for that reason: the night start was fine, but once caught in the morning rush on the side of a four-lane road, they no longer felt safe [9].

Under the 2024 rules the marathon limit is 6 hours 30, and marathoners who have not reached a checkpoint by the 3-hour-30 mark must stop and are taken back to the start on the race's buses. The half marathon has 3 hours 30, the 10 km 2 hours and the 5 km 1 hour 30 [3]. The 2026 map gives the same 6 hours 30 for the marathon, with a 10am cut-off [5].

sections.heading: Race Weekend Logistics
paragraphs: In 2025, race packs were collected at the That Luang grounds on 12 and 13 December, 10am to 6pm [2]; the 2024 rules did not allow anyone to collect a pack on another runner's behalf [3]. Entries are non-refundable [2], and in 2024 they could not be transferred [3].

Through World's Marathons, the 2025 fees were €60 for the marathon, €52 for the half, €35 for the 10 km and €13 for the 5 km, with minimum ages of 18, 16 and 12 for the three longer races [2]. The listed entry included a finisher medal, event T-shirt, single-use timing chip, pacers, a photo service, drink and nutrition stations, medical cover and toilets [2]. In 2024, prizes went five deep for men and women overall and in each age category, decided on gun time [3].

sections.heading: Should You Enter the 2026 Race?
paragraphs: Yes, if you want an unhurried capital-city marathon in cool December air, and you are comfortable finishing on open roads.

Think twice if you need closed roads, or will be out on the course long after 6.30am: under the 2024 rules, a five-hour marathoner runs the last two hours with traffic fully back [3]. The 3.30am start also means an early night.

The 2026 race is on Sunday 6 December [10]. The organiser's 2026 map keeps the 3.30am marathon start with a 10am cut-off, the half marathon at 4.30am with an 8am cut-off and the 10 km at 5am with a 7.30am cut-off [5], and packs are collected at the That Luang grounds on 4 and 5 December [9]. Check the road arrangements for 2026 before you book.
Nobody from this site ran the race. This review draws on a news report, the organiser's race information, rules and course maps, a race listing, airport weather records and one runner's account.

faqs.question: What time does the Vientiane International Marathon start?
faqs.answer: Very early. In 2025 the marathon started at 3.30am, the half marathon at 4.30am, the 10 km at 5am and the 5 km at 6am, from the That Luang grounds. The organiser's 2026 map keeps the same starts for the three longer races, with cut-offs of 10am, 8am and 7.30am.

faqs.question: Are the roads closed for the Vientiane International Marathon?
faqs.answer: Not fully. The organiser's 2024 rules say the route is shared during the race and fully reopened to traffic after 6.30am, three hours into the marathon. A runner at the 2022 race quit after being caught in morning rush-hour traffic on the side of a four-lane road. Slower marathoners should expect traffic.

faqs.question: What is the weather like at the Vientiane International Marathon?
faqs.answer: Cool for Southeast Asia. On race morning in 2025, Vientiane's Wattay airport recorded 20°C, a dew point of 17°C and 83% humidity at 6am, with mist and almost no wind. It reached only 23°C by 10am. Rain and drizzle fell the evening before, and mist lingered until about 7.30am.

faqs.question: What is the cut-off time for the Vientiane International Marathon?
faqs.answer: Six and a half hours for the marathon under the 2024 rules, with a check at the three-and-a-half-hour mark: runners who have not reached it must stop and ride a race bus back to the start. The half marathon had 3 hours 30. The 2026 map sets the marathon cut-off at 10am.

faqs.question: How much does the Vientiane International Marathon cost?
faqs.answer: In 2025, entries through World's Marathons cost €60 for the marathon, €52 for the half marathon, €35 for the 10 km and €13 for the 5 km. Entry included a finisher medal, event T-shirt, timing chip and photo service. Registration is non-refundable, and the 2024 rules did not allow transfers.

editorial_notes: Rewritten 2026-09-28 about the previous edition (14 December 2025). Material is thin: one news report on the 2025 race, an archived 2025 race listing, the organiser's 2024 rules and maps, the 2026 maps and airport weather. The 2025 results (Checkpoint Spot results site) returned HTTP 403 and were not read, so no finishing times or field depth are given. No 2025 course map is posted; the 2024 and 2026 maps show the same routes. Road reopening, cut-offs, transfer and prize rules are from the 2024 rules and are labelled as such. Weather is from airport METAR observations; the airport has no readings between midnight and 6am. The runner's account is from the 2022 race. No rating.
